title: Share shopping lists with household members
summary: Shopping lists can be shared with other members of a household.
A new household_members table links users to a household.
The list screen shows who added each item.
Shared lists update for everyone through the existing polling.

entries.author: Alex Rivera
entries.goal: People in the same household can see and edit one shopping list together.
scope: Members of a household share one shopping list
Any member can add and edit items
The list shows who added each item
out_of_scope: Real-time sync: the existing polling is enough for now
builds_on: The existing lists API and its polling

items.purpose: Which users belong to which household
The user who added each item
Every list a household can see
Household members can edit, not just the owner

entries.author: Alex Rivera
entries.question: Should a user be able to belong to more than one household?
entries.answer: One for now. Keep the table shaped so many is possible later.
entries.context: Many households changes every list query to need a household picker.
entries.cost: High. Schema and every list query.

entries.author: Alex Rivera
entries.question: Can any household member delete a shared list, or only its creator?
entries.answer: Only the creator can delete. Anyone can edit items.
entries.context: Deleting loses everyone's items, so it stays with one person.

entries.author: Alex Rivera
entries.question: How should the API say who added an item?
entries.decision: An added_by object with the user's id and display name on each item.
entries.why: The screen needs the name, and one request is cheaper than a lookup per item.
alternatives: Only the user id, with a separate users request
entries.cost: Medium. The response shape is a contract with the app.

entries.author: Sam Lee
entries.reason: The display name changes when a user renames themselves, so caching it in the item response goes stale.
entries.question: How should the API say who added an item?
entries.decision: Only added_by_id on each item, plus a members list on the household.
entries.why: The app already has the household's members, so names stay current.
alternatives: Keep the name on each item
entries.cost: Medium. The response shape is a contract with the app.

entries.author: Alex Rivera
entries.question: Where should the household check live?
entries.decision: In canEditList, next to the existing owner check.
entries.why: Every route already calls it, so nothing can skip the check.

entries.author: Alex Rivera
entries.question: How should the item row show who added it?
entries.decision: The person's initials in a small circle at the end of the row.
entries.why: The full name crowded the row on phones.

entries.author: Alex Rivera
entries.noticed: The list query loads every item and then filters out checked ones in code.
entries.why_not_done: It was like that before this branch and isn't part of sharing.
entries.follow_up: Filter checked items in the query.

entries.author: Alex Rivera
entries.behaviour: A household member can edit items but can't delete the list
